newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper to test support at $2,250.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper to test support at $2,250.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
A downside copper chart close on Thursday, rising London Metal Exchange stocks and a narrowing of nearby backwardations is likely to prompt a test of $2,250 a tonne, traders and chartists said.
Aluminium is likely to consolidate before heading higher, they added.
COPPER - Chart pressure is likely to see prices move to test support at $2,250 a tonne, traders and analysts said on Friday.
"Closed right on support at $2,270 and likely to head lower as the downside pressure increases, support seen at $2,250 and $2,226," LME brokers Brandeis said.
Harry Creates of Amalgamated Trading (AMT) said Thursday's downside close indicated a test of trendline support at $2,240 and possibly lower.
Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff was also suggesting copper prices would head lower.
"The close on the lows and a potential bearish flag developing does not bode well, as we look for further weakness to test this week's low at $2,256 and then $2,226 on a confirmed break."
On the upside, Creates said a close above $2,300 was initially needed to rekindle upside sentiment.
At 0735 GMT three months LME copper was quoted at $2,255/60, against Thursday's late close of $2,262/67.

ALUMINIUM - Seen consolidating before heading higher. "The market is establishing a base around $1,685/$1,700 and provided that this continues then further strength could be seen in due course," brokers Brandeis said.
Creates of AMT said the market was trying to consolidate between $1,688 and $1,730 before breaking higher. But if $1,688 breaks, falls to $1,665 could be seen, Creates added.
At 0735 GMT three months aluminium was quoted at $1,703/06, against $1,698/$1,702.
